fp4_expert_experiment.served_mode: Original FP4 verifier. The split-K trial changes accumulation order.

draft_target_overlap.method: Fixed observed greedy-draft trajectory. p is the post-sampler target probability vector. q is the normalized temperature-one softmax of the highest k DSpark logits at the same prefix. expected_accept sums min(p,q) over tokens and contexts. conditional_on_observed_token sums min(1,q(token)/p(token)) for the recorded target draws. Neither is a live throughput measurement. Second-position contexts only include rounds where the first greedy token matched.

two_first_token_branches.method: One uncached request per variant. Target layout was [anchor, primary, primary continuation, alternative]. The alternative attends only to its ancestors; its convolution uses the anchor and prefix. The fixed runs consume the same target token sequence as the live linear control. The shadow evaluates the alternative but never selects it. Promotion reuses the selected KV cell, convolution snapshot and target features without a second target decode.

two_first_token_branches.limitations: Changing the verifier shape or physical KV location can change logits. Fixed-path experiments compare cost and pass count; they do not establish equality of sampling distributions. Prototype was not deployed.

first_block.reference: Float32 reconstruction from original BF16 draft weights with the serving GGUF target output and embedding.

bench.method: Sequential native Windows llama-server HTTP requests with one slot, no cached prompt, and a fresh test process per run. Throughput is server decode speed. Generated token counts include reasoning. CUPTI and phase diagnostics are separate runs.
bench.cases: ds uses DSpark depth two. Other cases use --spec-type draft-dflash2 with LLAMA_EXPERIMENTAL_SPARK_DFLASH2=1. The number after prob or d is the number of proposals. prob enables --spec-draft-sampling probabilistic. native keeps the trained eight-position draft block. fuse enables LLAMA_EXPERIMENTAL_SPARK_CONTROL_PROJECT. adapt enables LLAMA_EXPERIMENTAL_DFLASH2_ADAPTIVE and LLAMA_EXPERIMENTAL_DFLASH2_TIMED_COST. compact enables LLAMA_EXPERIMENTAL_SPARK_COMPACT_ROUTES. q8 uses Q8_0 draft weights. All other DFlash2 cases use BF16 draft weights.

dflash2_expert_occupancy.method: Inkling DFlash2, seven probabilistic proposals, shared 20580 MiB cap and request 0. Captured input tensors and FP4 reference outputs for the seventh full eight-position verification pass with CUDA graphs disabled, then replayed the same 96 projections in four rotated orders. The diagnostic reserved 192 MiB of temporary GPU memory outside the engine ledger and used 131309568 bytes. Full HTTP tests enabled normal CUDA graphs and did not allocate the capture arena. A is variant 0, B is variant 2. Cold process order A1 B1 B2 A2. Warm order B then A, one unmeasured seed-44 request after server load before seed 42 and 43. For HTTP timings the stock and manual servers were left running and had unchanged activity counters across each measured request.
dflash2_expert_occupancy.result: All replay outputs were bitwise exact. The first fresh control was slow; the warmed control decoded faster than the singleton path on both seeds, with equal visible answers, reasoning hashes and token counts. Keep the experimental kernel out of the serving configuration.

dflash2_block_verification.method: Native Windows llama-server, seven sampled proposals, default temperature 1, no prompt cache. One seed-44 warm-up in each timing process. Same binary and target sampler settings for control and block. Outputs can differ for the same seed because the coupling consumes random draws differently. Target distributions for hypothetical prefixes were evaluated with a cloned sampler. Audit expectations use identical proposed paths and target probabilities with no timing claims. Counts include the correction or bonus and ignore early EOS in theoretical yield.
dflash2_block_verification.two_token_law: Four enumerated binary cases covering identical, disjoint and prefix-dependent probabilities, plus the published expected acceptance of 11/9 in its example.
